prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part prize on B028 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific arc is complete and independently confirmed: proglucagon processing and the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and the extra-pancreatic actions, then long-acting agonists with randomised outcome evidence in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Maturity is not in question. I did not change my configuration from round 1. The chair's first question has the most weight for me. I would answer that the citation should honour the physiology and the identification of the active peptide, and should name the therapeutic consequence only as the reason the discovery matters. That reading is the one that keeps the credited trio and the wording consistent with each other. A prize for discoveries of benefit to humankind has most often rewarded the step that opened the field, and here that step is the hormone biology.
statement.case_against: The weakness is credit, and round 1 did not remove it. Habener is outside the credited names and every trio is open to challenge on that ground. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested and I cannot settle it from the supplied text. Knudsen's analogue work is what reached patients, and Linnarsson makes a serious argument that it needed new insight and was not routine engineering. If a majority prefers a therapy-oriented citation, this configuration would honour the physiology and leave out the drug-development step that made it a medicine. I also note that five of six of us choosing the same trio is not evidence about the correct attribution.

responses.point: Converting native GLP-1, with a half-life of minutes, into a once-weekly agent required new insight into albumin binding and DPP-4 resistance, so Knudsen's step is invention and not routine engineering.
responses.response: I accept the factual point and I no longer describe her contribution as merely translational, which my round-1 wording came close to doing. The difficulty for me is that the three-name limit forces a choice between two readings of the achievement, and the discovery chain Holst, Drucker and Mojsov stands without the analogues, whereas the analogues do not stand without the physiology. You also say you would not treat the choice as a matter of principle, which narrows the disagreement. I would reopen the third seat if at least four members want a therapy-centred citation, and in that case citation and trio must change together to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. Without that majority I hold the physiology reading.

responses.point: Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is documented well enough to justify credit, and excluding her risks an attribution error the field would remember.
responses.response: This moves me more than the count of members does. You answer my uncertainty on priority by pointing to what she identified and made, and not to who published first. I agree that the committee should judge the contribution itself. Her role in the active form is a discovery-level step on which later pharmacology depended, even where the Habener group's priority is argued. I therefore keep her in the third seat. The risk you raise about Habener remains, and I would say plainly in the committee's reasoning that his proglucagon and processing work is recognised and that the omission follows the three-name limit and not a judgment of his contribution. I still have to flag that this rests on documented credit in the supplied text and my unverified recollection.

responses.point: The objection to an industry-based laureate should concern the nature of the contribution and not the employer, since neither the rules nor precedent exclude it; Knudsen would be the first person he reconsiders if development is to be honoured.
responses.response: I agree that employer is not the criterion, and I withdraw any implication in round 1 that her industry position counted against her. The test is whether the contribution is a discovery or the optimisation of an established target. On that test her work is closer to the line than I first allowed, but the identification of the active peptide is a more basic step. Your approach of keeping Knudsen as the named alternative if the committee decides to honour development is one I share. I also agree that the citation should state that the award is for discovery, so that the omission is a principled choice.

responses.point: Including Mojsov resolves one attribution dispute by importing another, and the commercial footprint of the drug class and the long-term safety and durability after discontinuation are not fully settled.
responses.response: The first point is fair and it is why I describe the credit as unsettled and not as clean. But every alternative trio imports a dispute, since Habener's absence affects all of them. On the evidence we have, I prefer the choice that can be justified by what each person did. On durability and safety, I agree these are still being defined, but they concern long-term use and do not weaken the discovery of the hormone's physiology or the demonstrated clinical effect. I would not hold B028 for a year because of them. The commercial scale also should not count against the discovery, and the citation should be worded around the physiology to make clear that discovery, not sales, is what is honoured.

responses.point: The unfolded protein response is a clean basic-science option for a later prize, with a tidy attribution for Walter and Mori, and optogenetics has been honoured as a method opening a field.
responses.response: I still hold B020 as my alternative because the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, but I do not support adding it to this prize. B028 already uses all three names allowed, so a second part would need two further names and would exceed the cap of three unique people. I would also keep to my own earlier reservation that a B020 citation must be worded narrowly around the IRE1, HAC1 and XBP1 mechanism. On optogenetics, I do not accept the precedent argument for this year, because six credited names cannot be cut to three without excluding someone decisive.

uncertainties: Whether the supplied record supports Mojsov's priority for the active peptide against the Habener group, which I cannot verify and which rests partly on my own recollection.
Whether a majority wants a therapy-oriented citation. If so, the third name changes from Mojsov to Knudsen and the citation changes with it.
How Habener's absence should be recorded, as it affects every trio on B028.
Whether a B045 pair (June and Sadelain, with Rosenberg's separate lineage and Eshhar's omission noted) should be preferred as the next prize.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. Documented ties are a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard at Rockefeller and roughly twenty co-authored works with committee colleague Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy). Neither is credited on any shortlisted candidate and no shortlisted candidate overlaps my own research. No member has disclosed a conflict requiring recusal, and I see none.
